facts.fact_text: On 24 November 2007 a group of opposition politicians organised protest rallies in several Russian cities, including Moscow.
The protest rallies of 24 November 2007 were part of a public campaign "[f]or the consolidation of democratic forces in order to defend the Constitution and the legal order".
On 24 November 2007 the applicants attended a gathering on Academician Sakharov Prospekt.
The gathering on Academician Sakharov Prospekt on 24 November 2007 had been organised by the second applicant.
The gathering on Academician Sakharov Prospekt on 24 November 2007 had been approved by the authorities.

According to the applicants, at 3 p.m. on 24 November 2007, at the end of the gathering on Academician Sakharov Prospekt, the applicants started walking to the location of another authorised gathering on Chistoprudnyy Boulevard.
The authorised gathering on Chistoprudnyy Boulevard took place between 2 p.m. and 4 p.m. on 24 November 2007.
On their way from Academician Sakharov Prospekt, which ran past Myasnitskaya Street, the applicants also intended to take a petition to the Central Electoral Committee.
The first applicant testified that he had been arrested while walking alongside other people from one authorised gathering to another on 24 November 2007.
The first applicant denied that there had been an organised march on 24 November 2007.
The second applicant alleged that he had been arrested while walking from the authorised meeting on Academician Sakharov Prospekt to the metro station on 24 November 2007.
The applicants' route on 24 November 2007 was blocked by the riot police.
The applicants were arrested on 24 November 2007.
Excessive force was allegedly used against the applicants at the time of their arrest on 24 November 2007.
